newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude likely to look again at support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude likely to look again at support.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ Yesterday's drop opens way to re-test of range lows for NYMEX crude and products, chartists said.
+ But a significant breakthrough on the downside after recent congested trade may not emerge, putting a floor in place for more buying
NYMEX oil futures are likely to return to the lows of recent ranges, although a full-blooded selloff is not necessarily on the cards, dealers and technical analysts said on Thursday.
Double bottoms are already in place on crude and heating oil continuation charts which if they hold again will reinforce the view that the worst of this year's drop may now be over.
"It will be bullish if it holds," said Gerald Samuels of ARB oil. "There will be a pretty decent triple bottom in place."
Samuels identified a congested trading range for crude between $18.96 and $20.10 a barrel for the last 12 sessions.
Crude's 48 cents drop to $19.35 a barrel on Wednesday still left the double bottom at $18.96 intact.

Yesterday's down move had left a residue of more bearish sentiment formed by the view of a three-day mini-downtrend, although Samuels also noted that others were viewing the 12-day period of congestion from the 84-cent drop of April 2 as a gentle uptrend.
Below the $18.96 mark was reasonably uncharted territory with "very critical support" around $18.75/80 from August last year on front month charts, he said.
But chartists were reluctant to predict sharp losses.

Samuels noted that trading volume on the downside moves had not been remarkable, while Cliff Green of Trend Analysis in England, setting the market in the longer/medium term, saw a different perspective.
"It's now getting to a point which is more interesting from the buyer's point of view," said Green of NYMEX crude.
Looking at monthly charts he saw an uptrend from 1994 still in place, challenged but not broken by recent lows.
"We could move marginally lower to around $18.75/80 based on an extension of the downward cycle from January but we're currently at a terminal phase of that cycle," Green said.
Between now and the early summer Green expected a correction to this year's drop, consolidation and then a probe towards $21.
The prospect for products futures echoed that of crude, analysts said.
Gasoline dropped a hefty 1.52 cents to close at 60.38 cents a gallon on Wednesday, but still left the recent low of 59.60 cents unhurt.
"59.60 is significant," said Samuals. "There have been a few breakdowns but we have not yet seen a settlement under 60 cents (basis May)."
A break of 59.60 would lead to a bearish 57.00, he said.
